title: Merging game mechanics to refresh games
author: Phumeinhaler
selftext:
Hi, I had a thought. With people merging 2 games together lately and remake/remasters as something game companies have been doing for the last decade or so why not have AI help improve our old favourites?

I've been playing video games for most of my life and the nostalgia always holds a game higher than it is if I went back to it... Mainly due to the controls being so poor or the improvement of the controls in late installments.

So my thought would be, what if we started using AI to take controls from one game, either the latest installment or a game from the same genre, and 'updated' the older game. 

An easy example could be a current monster hunter installment controls placed into an earlier one. Not only for the player controls but maybe the enemies as well. 

Or maybe taking a combat system from one game and putting into a different game. As just two games off the top of my head would be Dawnwalker's combat into Legacy of Kain games. 

Just a thought.

comments.author: Entropydemic
comments.body: I can hardly deny my excitement for this very subject. I saw this guy one to one Resident Evil 2 with Doom overnight and he had little to no experience.

comments.author: count023
comments.body:
I took an old star trek game from the interplay days, used its assets and are making a 16v16 dogfighting sim that acts just like the originals spaceflight Sim from the dos days.

You don't have to constrain yourself to just recent games.

replies.author: Phumeinhaler
replies.body: Exactly. That sounds great! Do you have a screen cap or gameplay video to see yours in action?

replies.author: count023
replies.body:
I can do one better, a few videoes of what i've done so far:   
[https://files.catbox.moe/nd3l4n.mp4](https://files.catbox.moe/nd3l4n.mp4)  
[https://files.catbox.moe/xhl0pn.mp4](https://files.catbox.moe/xhl0pn.mp4)  
[https://files.catbox.moe/umkv4m.mp4](https://files.catbox.moe/umkv4m.mp4)  


First two vides were VFX and sound efects testing, making sure the game played out like it did originally with the default details (combat AI, timers, dps, etc...) Third video was me rewriting the AI to support team based battles, using player assets to represent AI players too, so they all were legitiamtely fighting each other. Currently i'm building game modes and trialling peerjs and a few other multiplayer means so players can play each other, so far got 16v16 teams. And it's all playing using 18hgz to match DOS frame rates, the only assets i couldnt reuse verbatim were the MIDIS because browsers dont play midi anymore, so i had to render the original trakcs out as MP3s using MUNT but they sound just like they did from the OG game.
